payload.task_text:
You are the academic assessment coordinator responsible for monitoring quiz performance across multiple courses. You have been asked to analyze two courses that share a similar student population: Creative Computing and Culture from Fall 2014 (course ID 7) and Data-Driven Design from Spring 2013 (course ID 11). Both courses have quizzes and the department needs a comprehensive performance review.

All the quiz data (courses, quizzes, and per-student submission scores) is available through the Canvas MCP tools. Use `canvas_list_courses` (and `canvas_get_course`) to confirm the course names for course IDs 7 and 11, use `canvas_list_quizzes` to list the quizzes in each course, and use `canvas_list_quiz_submissions` to retrieve every student's submission score for a quiz (each submission row includes a `score` column).

Start by retrieving all quizzes and their submission scores for course 7 and course 11. For each quiz in each course, calculate the average score and the pass rate, where passing means scoring 70 or above. Express Pass_Rate as a percentage in the range 0-100 (for example 62.91, not 0.6291).

Write and run a Python script that processes the quiz data. The script should identify which quizzes have an average score below 75 and flag them for intervention. It should also compute the overall average across all quizzes from both courses combined and determine the performance gap between the two courses (the difference in their course-level averages).

Create a feedback survey titled "Academic Performance Self-Assessment" to gather student input. The survey needs exactly 5 questions. The first question should ask which course topics were most challenging (a free-text question). The second should ask how many hours per week the student spends studying, with choices "Less than 3", "3 to 5", "5 to 8", and "More than 8" (a single-choice / multiple-choice question). The third question should ask about preferred learning format with choices "Lectures", "Hands-on labs", "Group projects", and "Self-paced online" (a single-choice / multiple-choice question). The fourth question should ask the student to rate the overall course difficulty on a scale from 1 to 5, using a single-choice / multiple-choice question with the five options "1", "2", "3", "4", and "5". The fifth question should ask for suggestions for improvement (a free-text question).

For each quiz that has an average score below 75, schedule a one-hour review session in the calendar. Title each event "Quiz Review: [Quiz Title]" where the quiz title is the actual title of the quiz from the system. Schedule the first session on March 16, 2026 at 2:00 PM and each subsequent session one day later at the same time.

Create an Excel file called Quiz_Performance_Report.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be named "Quiz_Performance" with columns Course_ID, Course_Name, Quiz_ID, Quiz_Title, Avg_Score, Pass_Rate, and Needs_Review (Yes if average below 75, No otherwise). Include all quizzes from both courses. Write every numeric value (Avg_Score, Pass_Rate, Duration_Hours) as a literal number directly in the cells; do not write Excel formulas. The second sheet should be named "Feedback_Summary" listing the 5 survey questions with columns Question_Number, Question_Text, and Question_Type. The third sheet should be named "Remediation_Schedule" listing the scheduled review sessions with columns Quiz_Title, Session_Date, Start_Time, and Duration_Hours.

Finally, send an email from coordinator@assessment.example.com to faculty@assessment.example.com with the subject "Quiz Performance Analysis - Cross-Course Review". The email body should include the total number of quizzes reviewed across both courses, the number flagged for remediation, the overall program average score, and mention that the feedback survey has been created and review sessions have been scheduled.

Your workspace contains Program_Guidelines.pdf and analysis_config.json for reference.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent completes this bounded eleven-quiz task directly; do not dispatch sub-agents. Dynamically resolve the workspace, read Program_Guidelines.pdf and analysis_config.json, and preserve the task's literal course IDs, thresholds, dates, sender, recipient and subject.

Verify canvas_get_course(7) is CCC-2014J and canvas_get_course(11) is DDD-2013B. Call canvas_list_quizzes once per course and require IDs 20,21,22,23 for course 7 and 24,25,26,27,28,29,30 for course 11, retaining live quiz titles and points. Issue all eleven canvas_list_quiz_submissions calls in one native-parallel response. Deduplicate only by literal submission row.id, use numeric score rows, compute count/sum/average and score>=70 pass rate with a 0-100 denominator. Write and run analyze_quiz_performance.py once to create quiz_performance_results.json containing eleven quiz rows, submission-weighted course/program averages, absolute course gap and Needs_Review when average<75. Read both files back.

Create Academic Performance Self-Assessment exactly once, add the five stated questions sequentially in exact order/types/options, and get_form; never retry an ambiguous create. Freeze one packet containing the form receipt, eleven quiz rows, all summary metrics and flagged quiz schedule. Assign only flagged quizzes consecutive one-hour sessions from 2026-03-16 14:00 in quiz-ID order. Use a timezone only when analysis_config.json or the calendar environment exposes one; otherwise omit the override.

Then perform the three independent outputs directly with native-parallel batches:

- Sole-write Quiz_Performance_Report.xlsx with exactly the three requested sheets, eleven quiz rows, five survey rows and one schedule row per flagged quiz; use literal values and read every populated range back.
- Paginate Sent search/read candidates for exact coordinator@assessment.example.com -> faculty@assessment.example.com and subject Quiz Performance Analysis - Cross-Course Review. Send at most once after canonical totals exist, then read back.
- Search all flagged exact title/start/end events together, block duplicates, create all missing events once together, and get_event all retained IDs together. Each title is Quiz Review: [live quiz title].

Final reconciliation uses external workbook, form, email and event read-backs. No audit/repair wave is allowed.

You are helping an academic assessment coordinator gather complete quiz submission data for course ID 7 "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)" from the Canvas MCP API. The data must be complete (no truncation) because we will compute averages and pass rates.

BACKGROUND:
- Course 7 has 4 quizzes: quiz_id 20 "CMA 24295", 21 "CMA 24296", 22 "CMA 24297", 23 "CMA 24298".
- Each quiz is backed by an assignment: quiz 20 -> assignment 65, quiz 21 -> assignment 66, quiz 22 -> assignment 67, quiz 23 -> assignment 68.
- The endpoint `canvas_list_student_submissions` (mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions) returns paginated submission rows (each has `assignment_id`, `score`, `workflow_state`, `user_id`, and `pagination` metadata with `total_pages`/`has_more`). It is paginated: use `per_page=100` and iterate `page` from 1 until `pagination.has_more` is false. Total for this course is ~59 pages.
- IMPORTANT: If a single tool response is large, it may be truncated at ~100000 chars and saved to a file under /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-gform-gcal-excel-email/workspace/.tool_results/. The truncated files END with a marker "full_output_path: ..." which points OUTSIDE your allowed workspace — do NOT try to read that path (it will be blocked). Instead, only trust the portion of the JSON array that is complete. Because responses are capped, prefer keeping `per_page=100` (each page is ~59K chars, under the cap) so every page response is fully visible to you.
- You have a Python execution tool (mcp__local__python_execute) and filesystem tools. You may save intermediate JSON to /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-gform-gcal-excel-email/workspace/.

TASK:
1. Call canvas_list_student_submissions for course_id=7, assignment_ids=[65,66,67,68], per_page=100, page=1, then page=2, ... until pagination.has_more is false. Collect every submission row (assignment_id, user_id, score, workflow_state).
2. Aggregate by assignment_id and map to quiz: {65:20, 66:21, 67:22, 68:23}. Only include submissions that have a numeric score (workflow_state 'graded'). For each quiz compute:
   - n_submissions
   - avg_score = mean of all scores
   - pass_rate = (count of scores >= 70) / n * 100 (percentage 0-100)
   - needs_review = avg_score < 75
3. Write a JSON file to /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-canvas-gform-gcal-excel-email/workspace/course7_stats.json containing:
   {
     "course_id": 7,
     "course_name": "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)",
     "quizzes": [
        {"quiz_id": 20, "title": "CMA 24295", "assignment_id": 65, "n_submissions": ..., "avg_score": ..., "pass_rate": ..., "needs_review": ...},
        ... (all 4 quizzes)
     ],
     "course_avg_score": <mean of the 4 quiz avg_scores>
   }
   Use avg_score and pass_rate rounded to 2 decimals.
4. Also verify completeness: report how many total submission rows you collected per quiz and confirm no page was skipped.

DELIVERABLE: Return a concise summary listing, for each quiz: quiz_id, title, n_submissions, avg_score, pass_rate, needs_review, and the course-level average. Confirm the JSON file path written.
Fetch course 7 quiz submissions
